detection.description: What automatic license detection found for one URL of the schema: where the license was read (a repository commit or an exact package version), the files read and their digests.

url.description: An http(s) URL of printable ASCII without credentials.

detections.description: Findings of automatic license detection for the URLs no rule decides, sorted by url.

redirects.description: The documents of the schema that were served through an HTTP redirect, sorted by url without duplicates. The rules and detections cover each target as well; preparation reuses the decision only while every such URL still redirects to the recorded target with the recorded digest.

rules.description: IDs of the license rules that allowed the source and its dependencies, sorted.

redirect.description: A document of the schema that another URL served through an HTTP redirect.

digest.description: Digest of the bytes the target served.

target.description: The URL that served the document after the redirect; it differs from url.

url.description: The requested URL: the root document's retrieval URL or a dependency's source.

redirectURL.description: An http(s) URL of printable ASCII without credentials or fragment.

revision.description: Catalog revision YYYYMMDD.HHMM: the UTC minute of a publication, with a date from 2000 to 9999 and a time from 00:00 to 23:59.

artifactRevision.description: Present only when the last change touched metadata only: the older revision that gave the entry its current artifact (added it or changed its content). Absent, it equals lastChangedRevision.

contentDigest.description: Digest of the prepared schema bytes. While it and noticeDigest stay the same, publication reuses the artifact in entry.

entry.description: The catalog entry exactly as the current catalog lists it, provenance included; for an excluded schema the entry it last had.

excludedRevision.description: Present when an explicit exclude rule removed the schema from the catalog: the revision that dropped it. The record keeps its last entry so its ID stays reserved; it is not part of the current catalog.

firstRevision.description: The revision that added the schema to the catalog: its first publication, or its return after an exclusion.

heldReason.description: Why the schema is held; present exactly when heldSinceRevision is.

heldSinceRevision.description: Present while the catalog keeps the entry and artifact unchanged because the schema could not be refreshed: the first published revision that kept it so. A later refresh ends the hold.

id.description: The schema ID; equal to entry.id.

lastChangedRevision.description: The revision that last changed the entry in any way: added it, gave it new content (schema bytes or notice) or new metadata.

licenseDecision.description: The license decision the entry was published with; absent when it names no rules, detections or redirects (a license a local source file declares for documents served without a redirect). Preparation reuses it, without asking automatic license detection again, while the source and dependency digests stay the ones in entry.provenance and every recorded redirect still leads to its recorded target.

noticeDigest.description: Digest of the notice text the artifact carries in its notice layer; absent when it has none. A change republishes the schema, so the published notice always matches the entry.

description: catalog/state.json, the record in Git of what the publisher has published. Constraints that JSON Schema cannot express are enforced by the publisher: the canonical encoding (member order, two-space indentation, a final newline), schemas sorted by id in strictly ascending byte order with id equal to entry.id, the entry rules of api/catalog.schema.json that it cannot express either, real calendar dates in revisions, firstRevision <= artifactRevision < lastChangedRevision <= catalog.revision, lastChangedRevision < heldSinceRevision <= catalog.revision, lastChangedRevision < excludedRevision <= catalog.revision, sorted license decision rules, detections and redirects, a redirect target that differs from its url, and SPDX license expression grammar.

catalog.description: The current catalog: its revision and the digest and size of its OCI image index, which clients pin.

recipe.description: The prepare recipe of the current catalog.

source.description: The upstream input of the current catalog.

repository.description: An https URL of printable ASCII without credentials, query or fragment.
